title: It didn’t kill you overnight.
paragraphs: And now you carry it like it’s part of your identity.

You smile in public.
You serve in church.
You post verses.
And here’s the question you can’t escape:
What do you do when the problem isn’t around you… but inside you?

Not as a concept.
Not as a sermon.

“My guilt has overwhelmed me like a burden too heavy to bear.”
— Psalm 38:4

Not “I feel bad.”
Not “I made a mistake.”

This is not fake guilt.
This is not religious anxiety.

This is what happens when a soul becomes fully aware:
“I have sinned against a holy God.”

Your strength fades.
Your peace disappears.
Your mind won’t rest.
Even your body feels it.

Psalm 38:3 says,
“There is no soundness in my flesh because of your indignation… no health in my bones because of my sin.”

Into your thoughts.
Into your sleep.
Into your relationships.
Into your body.
You can hide it from people.
But you cannot hide it from your soul.
And here’s where it gets uncomfortable.

Not his enemies.
Not his circumstances.
Not his past.

He says in Psalm 38:18,
“I confess my iniquity; I am troubled by my sin.”
And that’s the line most people refuse to cross.

Because as long as you explain your sin,
you never have to repent of it.

As long as you justify it,
you never have to surrender it.

As long as you rename it,
you never have to face it.

“It’s just stress.”
“It’s just how I cope.”
“It’s just who I am.”
But heaven calls it something else.
And sin is not just breaking rules.

It’s choosing self over God.
Desire over obedience.
Darkness over light.

Romans 3:23 says,
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.”
That means the quiet sinner… and the public one.
But here’s the tension that most people miss:
Because it tells you something is wrong before it destroys everything.

2 Corinthians 7:10 says,
“Godly sorrow brings repentance that leads to salvation without regret.”
There is a sorrow that leads to death.
And there is a sorrow that leads to life.

Scroll it away.
Drink it away.
Laugh it away.
You can bring it to God.

Psalm 38:9,
“O Lord, all my longing is before you; my sighing is not hidden from you.”
And this is where everything turns.

Because the moment you stop running from God…
you discover something shocking:
He is not running from you.
This is where Psalm 38 points forward.
Because David carried guilt he could not remove.
But Jesus came to carry guilt that was not His own.

Isaiah 53:5 says,
“He was pierced for our transgressions… crushed for our iniquities… the punishment that brought us peace was on Him.”
The weight crushing David in Psalm 38…
Was placed fully on Christ at the cross.

Every hidden sin.
Every secret habit.
Every shame you buried.
And Jesus didn’t just feel your guilt.
He absorbed the wrath your sin deserved.

On the cross, He cried,
“My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?” (Matthew 27:46)
So you wouldn’t have to be.
So your guilt would not be your grave.
So your shame would not be your identity.
Here is the Gospel, clear and unshakable:

You are more sinful than you want to admit.
But in Christ, you are more loved than you can imagine.
But by repentance and faith in Jesus Christ alone.

1 John 1:9 says,
“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us… and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.”
What are you still carrying that Jesus already died for?
You don’t need a better excuse.
Because the same God who convicts…
Right now—yes, right now—you can do what David did.
Type “OPEN MY HEART” if you’re ready to stop hiding.
